subject: POC readout + model commitment roadmap and next owners
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@shoply.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: POC readout + model commitment roadmap and next owners

Hi Elena — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a proposed POC roadmap so we can lock scope and owners this week. I pasted a short mutual action plan at the bottom.

High-level ask from your team (from call)
- Validate classification and response quality for returns & refunds flow in US, IT (Italian), and ES (Spanish) locales.
- Meet latency target for synchronous UI calls (goal: median <= 400ms).
- Evaluate safety/regression on edge prompts (fraud/PII extraction).

Proposed model lineup for trial (our recommendation)
- Primary (open): Llama-2-Chat-13B, quantized 8-bit (good balance of quality + latency)
- Fallback: Mistral-Instruct-7B q4_0 (lighter, faster and cheaper for low-risk queries)
- Embeddings: OpenAI-like model (open-embedding-1024) or Redwood-embed-2 (if you want local control)

Why this set? Llama-2-Chat 13B gives the best quality consistency across English + Romance languages. Mistral provides a cost/latency fallback for high-throughput non-sensitive lookups. We can tune instruction prompts and provide a prompt ensemble for locale-specific fallbacks.

Evaluation plan (short)
- Acceptance metrics: intent accuracy >= 88% (macro), response precision for refund policy language >= 92% on labeled test set, latency median <= 400ms, 95th percentile latency <= 900ms.
- Test assets: we propose running your curated prompt set (attached) + a dynamically collected 1k post-demo samples during week 1.
- Quality gates: any drop >3% in intent accuracy vs baseline triggers rollback to fallback config and 24-hour post-rollout freeze.

Resources and ownership
- Redwood: POC orchestration, model hosting, telemetry dashboards (Soojin)
- Redwood (infra/ops): inference config, batching profiles, KV cache setup (Connor)
- Shoply: labeled test set, acceptance sign-off (Elena + Product)

Timeline (proposed)
- 6/7: sign-off on scope + SOW (email confirmation)
- 6/10–6/16: test assets prepared + baseline run in sandbox
- 6/17–6/23: internal tuning + parallel run against fallback
- 6/24: acceptance readout + final decision

Attachments: redwood_poc_plan_v1.pdf (POC SOW draft), shoply_prompt_set_v2.csv (seed prompts), redwood_model_matrix.xlsx (latency/cost estimates)

Please reply with any scope changes and confirm if the model lineup looks OK for the Shoply product team. If you want a heavier model (30B) for higher-fidelity language generation in Italian we can discuss, but it will increase latency/cost.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee | Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC readout + model commitment roadmap and next owners

Thanks Soojin — this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few notes: 

1) Scope: confirmed US + IT + ES. For Italian we have a handful of legal phrasing cases where fidelity matters — if Llama-2-Chat-13B struggles we may ask for a canary with a 30B model for those queries only.

2) Security: we need a short SOC2 evidence packet and clarification on data retention for sandbox logs. Can your team share a SOC2 summary or point us to the folder?

3) Timeline: 6/7 sign-off is tight for our procurement — will aim for an internal OK but please be prepared for 6/9 as fallback.

OK to proceed on your proposed lineup for the POC, contingent on SOC2 note and SOW updates that indicate data retention is 30 days in the sandbox.

Elena
Elena Rossi | Head of Product, Shoply
elena@shoply.com

Elena — quick technical clarifications from infra side: 

- SOC2 evidence: we have a short summary and the audit readiness checklist in the Drive link I added to the hub (I'll share the exact file in the folder you requested). For sandbox logs, default retention is 30 days; we can extend to 90 days for the trial if you need it but it will affect storage costs.

- Inference config suggestion: start with continuous batching with max batch size 32 and dynamic batch timeout 6ms for Llama-2-Chat-13B 8-bit. KV cache enabled for session continuity. For the fallback Mistral-7B use batch size 64 and lower top_p to 0.95 for terser output.

- Canary setup for Italian legal phrases: we can route only those prompts to a 30B canary model (dedicated route) so most traffic stays on the 13B model. That minimizes cost but gives the fidelity you need.

I'll drop a short readme to the shared Drive with the inference parameters.

Connor O'Brien
Infra Lead, Redwood Dedicated
